text:
sam: quick q about embeddings endpoint behavior when we get mixed inputs (bytes, strings, empty) — we're seeing an edgecase in the ingest job. how should truncation/sentinels be handled?

lee: do you mean: mixed types in the same batch payload, e.g. ["utf8 str", base64(bytes), null]? or different content-length distributions?

sam: mixed types in same array. current runtime silently coerces bytes -> utf8 when possible, otherwise it throws. also some long items are getting truncated but we don't tag them in the response. want to align with contract before we ship the ingester change.

anika: ok. two separate concerns: 1) input coercion rules, 2) truncation visibility & ordering guarantees across splits. i'd prefer explicit behavior for each input item. suggestions: return per-item metadata: {"truncated": true/false, "original_length": N, "encoding": "utf8"|"base64"|"bytes"} so clients can decide to re-split or fetch raw.

mike: +1 on metadata. minimal changes for backwards-compat: add optional top-level "item_meta" array in responses. old clients ignore it. new clients can opt-in. keep the primary response field (vectors) as-is to preserve indexes.

sam: does adding "item_meta" break ordering? we must guarantee vectors[i] corresponds to input[i] even when we split a big input into multiple internal chunks.

anika: vector index alignment must be stable. proposal: server-side splitting for very long single items returns multiple internal vectors but is flattened and merged back to a single output vector (e.g., prefix pooling) at the same index. if we ever return multiple vectors per input, that's a contract change and needs explicit flag.

lee: small edge: empty string vs null vs whitespace-only. what should endpoint do? current behavior: empty string -> zero-vector, null -> error 400. is that ok?

mike: i'd rather be explicit: null -> preserve null and include null in vectors array (and an item_meta entry with error="null_input"). empty string -> deterministic zero-vector + truncated=false. whitespace-only -> treat as string, compute embedding.

sam: that helps. what about truncation cutoff value? runtime uses token-budget of 8192 tokens per request right now, but for embeddings we should define max_input_bytes or max_items_per_batch. ops noticed some RPS spikes from huge batches.

anika: recommend: conservative defaults: max_items_per_batch=1024, max_total_payload_bytes=4_000_000 (~4MB). if exceeded, server returns 413 with a helpful body and item_meta for any accepted items. we can keep auto-splitting off by default; enable by header `X-Embed-AutoSplit: true` for clients that want server splitting.

lee: auto-split semantics? if enabled, server will split a single oversized item across multiple internal chunks, compute sub-embeddings, then aggregate back to 1 vector per input using average pooling by default. we should document aggregation strategy and allow param `aggregation=avg|max|first`.

mike: for backward-compat, default aggregation must be deterministic and documented. avg is fine. please add test vectors in compat suite. I'll add CI check.

ci-bot: compat check started for PR #4127 — embedding contract changes (item_meta + auto-split header). running: unit tests, integration (mock runtime), and e2e ingest flow.

sam: perfect. action items: anika to draft API response example and docs snippet; mike to add opt-in header handling and item_meta plumbing; lee to update ingester to pass X-Embed-AutoSplit when configured; sam to add a small e2e to catch null vs empty case. i'll open a single PR that wires doc + runtime + ingester TODOs.

anika: i'll drop a draft in the docs channel in ~1h. quick note for docs: include example request + response, e.g.:

```json
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "input": ["short text", "", null, "<very long text...>"]
}

RESPONSE 200
{
  "vectors": [[0.01, ...], [0.0, ...], null, [0.12, ...]],
  "item_meta": [
    {"truncated": false, "original_length": 12, "encoding": "utf8"},
    {"truncated": false, "original_length": 0, "encoding": "utf8"},
    {"error": "null_input"},
    {"truncated": true, "original_length": 120000, "encoding": "utf8", "aggregation": "avg"}
  ]
}
```

lee: nice. also callout: models with dynamic vector size? we must not return variable-length vectors for same model in same response. if we ever do compressed or pooled outputs we need explicit model variant and dims in response e.g. `vector_dim`.

mike: good catch. include `vector_dim` as top-level in response and assert vectors are either null or arrays of that length. CI will verify lengths.

sam: great. thanks everyone. i'll track in PR and ping when drafts are up. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: compat check passed for unit tests, integration failing on e2e due to old ingester not sending header. failing tests listed in the PR. :eyes:
